title: Review output noisy? Ask whether it's vague or inconsistent
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Many low-value comments, consistent run to run
Prompt says "be careful" or "high confidence only"
Real bugs caught only some runs
rule: Precision comes from explicit criteria about what counts as a finding. Few-shot examples are for making output consistent once the criteria exist.

title: Review findings are bad: is the rule vague, or the output inconsistent?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: One category mostly false positives; instruction is a vague goal
Criteria are concrete, but findings vary in shape or severity
Review misses flaws in its own code
Want to know which categories get dismissed
rule: Precision comes from categorical criteria. Turn 'keep X trustworthy' into 'flag only when claim and code disagree'.

title: Output is weak: is the standard missing, or applied unevenly?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Output is weak in the same way everywhere; prompt uses a vague word
Criteria are clear but output varies run to run
Many false positives in one category
Categorical criteria with concrete code examples
Generator reviews its own output and misses issues
Big change reviewed in one pass, uneven depth
Per-file passes plus an integration pass
rule: When output is consistently weak and the prompt says only "thorough" or "careful", write checkable criteria first. Reach for examples when criteria exist but are applied unevenly.

title: Model forced to guess: what's missing?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Model always commits, schema has no "unsure" option
Add a flag or "unclear" value + criteria
Flag exists but is used unevenly
Wrong value costs far more than a review
Two runs agree on a wrong value
Don't use agreement as a check
rule: If the model can only commit, it will guess. Add an "unsure" outcome, write criteria for using it, and route on it.

title: Review output is poor: is it noise or inconsistency?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Many findings in categories nobody wants; trust is low
Explicit criteria: what to report and what to skip
Same issue gets different format or severity each run
Don't know which categories are noisy
Generator misses its own subtle bugs
rule: To cut false positives, state exactly what to report and what to skip. Use examples for consistency, not for precision.

title: A review category is noisy: what fixes precision?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Noisy category is optional and trust is collapsing
Pause the category while it is rewritten
Don't know which patterns are false positives
Same finding gets different severity each run
rule: To cut false positives, define the category as specific, testable conditions with code samples. Pausing is only for optional checks.

title: Output includes too much: what sharpens it?
head: What you observe
Where the fault is
Fix
rows: Vague instruction, criteria can be stated
Boundary hard to describe in words
Unknown which items are false positives
rule: If you can write the categories down, write them down. Few-shot is for boundaries you can't easily describe and for consistency.

title: Too many false positives? Ask whether you can state the rule
head: Situation
Fix
Why
rows: One noisy category hides good findings
rule: If you can name what counts, write it as explicit criteria with a small example of each.

title: Too many false positives: what kind of fix does this category need?
head: What you observe
Cause
Fix
rows: Category has only a vague instruction
Criteria exist, borderline cases decided inconsistently
Category noisy and trust is collapsing; team can drop it for now
rule: No definition → write explicit criteria. Criteria exist but applied unevenly → add examples.
